description: **Debug/scratch tool** — for production code, use iris_doc_load to ensure source control and review. This tool writes content directly to IRIS without creating a file on disk, and is intended for one-off inspection, quick reproductions, or throwaway test classes only. A leading byte-order mark is stripped from the content before it is sent, and a write IRIS refuses (a non-empty result.status inside an HTTP 200 response) is returned as an error carrying IRIS's text; nothing is stored then. An existing document is saved only if it has not changed since this tool read its current version; ignoreConflict skips that check. For an existing class, a put whose content drops one of the class's Storage definitions is refused and nothing is stored, because IRIS would generate new storage at the next compile, which can change how existing rows are read; allowStorageRegeneration (default false) lets it through, and changing a Storage definition's content is always allowed.

allowStorageRegeneration.description: Boolean (true/false), default false. When false, a put to an existing class whose content drops one of the class's Storage definitions is refused and nothing is stored; changing a Storage definition's content is allowed. When true, the put goes ahead and IRIS generates new storage at the next compile, which can change how existing rows are read. No effect on a new class or on other document types.

content.description: Document content. Pass as a single string with newlines (preferred) or a JSON array of lines. The full class/routine source including 'Class ... {' header.

ignoreConflict.description: Boolean (true/false), default false. Not needed to replace an existing document: without it the tool reads the document's current version and saves only if it is still that version. When true, IRIS skips that version check.

server.description: Named server profile to target for this call (from `IRIS_PROFILES`). Omit to use the default server.

name: iris_doc_put
title: Put Document
